title: Mova: dependable local moto pickup
subtitle: A Rwanda-specific business model for an ASYV–Ntunga pilot
decision: Fund a small validation pilot, not a national rollout. The transport-access problem is credible; local demand, willingness to pay, permitted pricing and paid partnerships remain unproven.
pitch: Mova helps adults around ASYV and Ntunga request a licensed local moto, identify the correct plate, communicate pickup details and pay the driver after the trip. We start with one corridor, a small vetted driver roster and assisted booking through partner desks. We aim to earn an approved completed-trip service fee and institutional coordination subscriptions. We will expand only when pickup reliability, driver take-home earnings, repeat usage and fee collection meet measured targets.

sources.title: NISR — EICV7 Utilities and Amenities, 2023/24
sources.finding: Transport-stage access within 20 minutes: rural 17%, urban 54%. Home internet: rural 19%, urban 56%. These are household measures, not local demand or individual smartphone ownership.

sources.title: ASYV — visitor directions
sources.finding: Directions take visitors off the main road at Ntunga and onward for about nine kilometres. This supports a specific last-mile corridor, not a measured service failure rate.

sources.title: RURA — published transport tariffs
sources.finding: The regulator lists motorcycle fare decisions, including an August 2022 adjustment. Obtain the currently applicable rules for the corridor; do not treat an old notice as proof that unrestricted bargaining or a new fee is permitted.

sources.title: RURA — road transport services
sources.finding: RURA describes motorcycle operator authorization and cooperative requirements and encourages ICT use. Confirm the exact platform/operator category and requirements before public operation.

sources.title: YEGOMOTO — provider FAQ
sources.type: Competitor self-description; page contains legacy wording
sources.finding: Describes metering, cash/cashless payment, trip identifiers and complaint handling. Mova cannot claim these features are unique. Current Ntunga coverage and current competitor fees require field checks.

sources.title: Rwanda DPO — registration as controller/processor
sources.finding: Registration is required for intended controller/processor activity. The process can take up to 30 working days after a complete application; real-data launch depends on applicable approvals.

sources.title: Rwanda DPO — privacy FAQs
sources.finding: Location is personal data. Online hailing is included in covered activities; foreign storage/transfers require the applicable authorization. A cheap foreign server is not automatically a compliant choice.

sources.title: RDB/ORG — business registration
sources.finding: Online business registration itself is free. Advice, contracts, transport approvals, insurance and compliance work may still cost money.

sources.title: Google Maps Platform — core service prices
sources.finding: Model uses monthly 10,000 free events per relevant Essentials SKU, then USD 7/1,000 Dynamic Maps loads and USD 5/1,000 Compute Routes Essentials requests. SKU, taxes and provider terms must be checked before purchase; advanced routing can cost more.

sources.title: MTN Rwanda — data bundles
sources.finding: Lists 3 GB/30 days at RWF 3,000. The pilot's RWF 2,000 per-driver monthly allowance is a partial contribution, not a promise to cover all phone/data costs.

sources.title: RRA — VAT registration
sources.finding: Published mandatory thresholds include RWF 20 million in 12 months or RWF 5 million in three consecutive months. Have an accountant confirm taxable platform turnover and principal/agent treatment; passenger fare GMV is not automatically Mova revenue.

sources.title: RRA — VAT calculator
sources.finding: Shows an 18% standard VAT rate. The model has an editable VAT deduction assumption; its base case is before income tax and does not assert tax exemption.

sources.title: Connected entrepreneurship assignment — Business Model Canvas
sources.finding: Calls for all nine blocks, competitive analysis, visible presentation, a service simulation and audience Q&A.

sources.title: Connected nine-block canvas template
sources.finding: The conventional nine-block arrangement is preserved in the separate printable poster.

problem: Specific job: an adult at a dispersed institution, home or workplace needs a dependable connection to the Ntunga moto rank/main road, without walking to find a driver or repeatedly calling uncertain contacts.

Hypotheses to measure: wasted pickup-search time, unclear meeting points, avoidable no-shows and poor trip accountability. These are not established local statistics. The user's preference for discussing an offer is an idea to test, not proof that all Rwandans prefer bargaining.

The national access evidence and ASYV's published directions justify investigating the corridor. They do not establish how many local adults will use Mova, how often existing motos fail, or willingness to pay.

A map app cannot create road capacity or make an unavailable driver appear. The operational product is a vetted roster, honest availability, clear pickup communication and supported completion. The animated prototype is not evidence of actual pickup times or demand.

Do not lead with 'Rwanda has no moto apps', 'cashless payment is new', or 'we eliminate accidents'. Existing providers already offer overlapping features. The proposed distinction is dependable, locally supported pickup on a tightly defined corridor.

canvas.title: Key Partners
short: Licensed Ntunga moto cooperative/rank
Prospective institutional booking desks
RURA, district and privacy compliance contacts
Hosting/maps suppliers; payment providers if later integrated
detail: Contract with a licensed local cooperative or authorized operator; check each driver's permit, plate, insurance and passenger helmet. Do not buy motorcycles or employ unlicensed riders to make the pilot look active.

Seek permission from ASYV and other nearby workplaces/guesthouses for adult staff/visitor booking desks. They are prospective partners, not signed customers. Use school branding or grounds only with permission.
Consult RURA on platform licensing, fare rules and the proposed fee, and DPO on registration, location processing and hosting. Seek a qualified legal/accounting review.

Use a compliant hosting supplier and Google Maps where authorized. Start with rider-to-driver cash/MoMo after the ride; a future licensed payment partner would handle collection and reconciliation rather than Mova holding rider deposits.

canvas.title: Key Activities
short: Verify and train drivers
Coordinate reliable pickups and supported booking
Maintain secure app and trip records
Reconcile completed-ride fees; measure repeat usage
detail: Recruit a maximum of 20 pilot drivers; verify documents, train on accurate online status and the pickup-code sequence, and define daytime service windows and escalation responsibilities.

Offer Kinyarwanda-first onboarding with English available. Assist customers without smartphones through an authorized desk or phone contact; do not build an expensive USSD service before demand is proven.

Maintain HTTPS, real authentication, participant-scoped location access, monitoring and backups. Replace simulated driver movement with consented real updates before claiming live commercial tracking.

Reconcile only completed trips weekly with the cooperative, resolve errors transparently, and measure request-to-pickup time, completion, no-shows, incidents, repeat use, driver earnings and cash collection.

canvas.title: Key Resources
short: Existing prototype and accountable student team
Vetted driver roster and cooperation agreement
Borrowed phones and secure shared backend
Working capital and part-time human support
detail: The existing two-device prototype demonstrates the concept. It is not yet a verified-driver commercial service, payment system or insurance guarantee.
Two borrowed test phones, founder laptops, consented driver data, Kinyarwanda support materials and a documented service process keep capital needs low.
One part-time coordinator covers defined pilot windows. Founders and a mentor provide development and escalation time in kind; this is a real resource with an explicit replacement cost.
A ring-fenced RWF 2.85 million pilot envelope funds a limited experiment. Any extra permit or insurance requirement beyond reserves must be funded or the launch reduced/paused.

canvas.title: Value Propositions
short: Identify the right driver by plate
Confirm pickup and communicate directly
Transparent lawful fare; pay after riding
For drivers: incremental local demand
For institutions: coordinated bookings and records
detail: Passengers: a known plate, clear meeting point, honest driver status, communication and a post-trip payment sequence. A pickup code adds accountability; it is not a guarantee of physical safety.
Drivers: additional local requests and less avoidable search/empty travel, provided measured take-home income improves after all fees, fuel and data costs. No guaranteed earnings claim.
Institutions: a supported driver roster, an assisted booking route, a trip log and defined issue handling. Test whether these replace enough staff coordination work to justify a subscription.

Respect current fare and meter rules. Retain negotiated offers only where the applicable regulator permits them; otherwise show the lawful tariff/quote and retain pickup communication and choice of driver.

canvas.title: Customer Relationships
short: Kinyarwanda-first human onboarding
Saved preferred drivers and clear receipts
Defined support hours and issue handling
Weekly cooperative review; no misleading guarantees
detail: Onboard drivers face to face and show customers the complete service using the existing prototype. Ask about their current solution before promoting a new one.
Publish support hours and service boundaries. Log no-shows and complaints, suspend unsafe/unverified drivers through a documented process, and never imply a report summons emergency services.

Let adults repeat a preferred driver relationship, while keeping a dispatcher/roster useful when that driver is unavailable. Convenience and accountable records must earn repeat use; do not assume customers stay to pay a commission.
Discuss weekly earnings and collection with drivers and monthly results with each institutional buyer. Do not sell precise location histories or personal data as a revenue stream.

canvas.title: Customer Segments
short: First users: adults near ASYV–Ntunga
Adult staff, visitors and local workers
Supply: licensed local moto drivers
Paying buyers: drivers + institutional desks
No unaccompanied-minor pilot
detail: Start with adult staff, approved visitors, nearby workers and residents who actually make corridor journeys. Permission from the institution and local operator is required; this plan assumes no existing agreement.
Target 100 active adult customers as a testable acquisition goal, not an existing audience. At 15.6 completed rides/customer/month they would support the month-three volume assumption.

Drivers are supply partners and proposed fee payers. Institutional desk managers/budget holders are the second buyer group. Passengers pay the lawful transport fare to the driver and are not charged a separate assumed platform surcharge.
Exclude unaccompanied children and student transport from the first pilot. Do not present ASYV's entire population or Rwanda's population as reachable paying customers.

canvas.title: Channels
short: Mobile web app; low-data experience
Rank demonstrations and QR/web links
Authorized institution desk and phone assistance
Referrals and direct institutional sales
detail: Use the responsive web app rather than paying for separate native Android/iOS launches. Show route/status and plate selection but avoid repeated unnecessary map loads.
Acquire drivers through cooperative/rank meetings and passengers through permitted institutional demonstrations, posters and referrals. Broad paid social-media campaigns are outside the pilot budget.
Provide assisted booking by a permitted staff desk or a pilot phone contact for adults without smartphones. Budget limited support hours; do not promise a 24/7 call centre.

Sell the institutional service directly to a named budget holder using a short paid trial, agreed scope and renewal review. The institutional administration/reporting workflow can initially be manual; it is not already a finished app feature.

canvas.title: Cost Structure
short: Setup: RWF 880,000
Monthly pilot fixed/driver support: RWF 500,000
Variable provision: RWF 20/completed ride
90-day ceiling including contingency: RWF 2,844,640
Funding request rounded to RWF 2,850,000
detail: Keep the model asset-light: no motorcycle purchases, office lease, fleet fuel, large launch adverts or proprietary payment wallet. Existing vehicles/insurance remain the operator's responsibility, subject to verification.

Base cash operating budget is RWF 460,000/month plus RWF 2,000 data contribution for each of 20 drivers. Include actual human support and compliance work; a cheap website alone is not an operating business.
The RWF 20 per completed ride is a planning provision for incremental messaging/reconciliation and ordinary service errors, not a quoted payment-processing tariff or accident insurance.

Founder development/support time, borrowed devices and space are disclosed in-kind. Income tax, quoted extra permits/insurance, full-time salaries and a public launch are not silently covered by the pilot figures.

canvas.title: Revenue Streams
short: Proposed 8% fee on completed Mova trips only
RWF 75,000/month per institutional desk
No fare deposits or cancelled-trip fees
No ads/data sales assumed; grants are funding
Fees depend on permission and willingness to pay
detail: Illustrative average fare RWF 2,500 × proposed 8% = RWF 200 billed per completed trip. At 95% fee collection the cash receipt is RWF 190/trip. The RWF 2,500 is a modelling average, not a verified ASYV–Ntunga tariff.

Collect platform service fees from the driver/cooperative after completed trips, reconciled weekly. The passenger pays the driver after riding. Do not deduct money from uncompleted rides or treat driver fare receipts as Mova revenue.

Seek RWF 75,000/month for each institutional booking desk covering coordination, roster management and records within agreed hours. Base month three assumes two paying desks; none is currently committed.

Do not charge a new platform fee on top of an incumbent meter/platform obligation unless permitted and economically acceptable to drivers. If per-trip fees are rejected, test a partner-funded coordination contract; do not declare the same financial forecast still valid. Sponsorship/grants fund the experiment and are not recurring customer revenue.

setup: Estimate; founder implementation is separately in kind
Contracts, regulatory/privacy advice and compliance reserve
Allowance, not a quoted licence or insurance premium
Posters, consent/training materials and presentation print
fixed: Allowance; lawful hosting location/transfer approval required
Reserve; model estimates overage separately at higher volume
Limited pilot windows, not 24/7 coverage or a full salary
Field transport, referrals and local outreach
Operational administration / employer and service reserve
Not an insurance policy; confirm staffing obligations
validation: Interview 30 adult prospective passengers, 20 licensed drivers and 5 institutional budget holders. Observe 30 real pickup attempts across peak/off-peak periods, with consent.

At least 15/30 passengers describe a recent concrete pickup difficulty; independently log baseline median/p90 wait and the current alternative. If finding a moto is already easy, stop or change the segment.
Meet the relevant RURA/local operator contacts; confirm pricing/fee permissions, licensing, insurance and privacy requirements. Seek ASYV permission and one licensed operating partner.

No real-data/public trip launch until applicable approvals, coverage and operator responsibilities are clear. A 90-day calendar can slip; DPO registration alone can take up to 30 working days after a complete application.
Begin with assisted/manual coordination before a wider app launch. Offer limited daytime/peak windows, verify the roster, and track 100 completed trial trips.

At least 80% request completion, no-show rate below 10%, and a target 30% improvement in median pickup time versus the observed baseline. A serious safety incident triggers review/pause regardless of other metrics.
Show the proposed 8% driver service fee against measured incremental net earnings. Offer institutions an explicitly priced RWF 75,000/month service trial.
At least 10 drivers consent to the permitted fee, collection reaches 95%, and two institutions sign and actually pay before using the month-three subscription assumption.
Recruit toward 100 active adult users, measure cohorts rather than downloads, and compare driver total take-home after fuel, data and all existing fees.

Target 30% of first-time customers repeating within 30 days. By month three, show a credible route toward roughly four completed app trips per driver/day without discounts or worse driver earnings; otherwise reduce costs, change the payer, or stop.
questions: Why would someone use this instead of walking to the rank or calling a familiar driver?
Only if measured pickup reliability and saved coordination effort beat those options. Interviews and a manual pilot must show this; a map is not enough.
Does the problem matter in Rwanda?
Official household evidence indicates a transport-access gap, and ASYV has a real last-mile corridor. Neither proves demand for Mova specifically. We will not invent local survey results.
Why not launch nationally?
Small network density, human support and regulatory clarity matter more than nationwide downloads. One corridor keeps failure and spending contained.
Is bargaining definitely allowed?

No such claim is made. Applicable fare, meter and platform fee rules need confirmation. If bargaining is not allowed, remove it from commercial operation and retain compliant pricing and communication.
Why would drivers pay an 8% fee?
Only for incremental demand that improves take-home income after all existing charges. Eight percent is a test price, not a proven acceptable rate or regulatory approval.
How is the fee collected if passengers pay cash?

The driver keeps the fare at ride completion; Mova reconciles completed trips and invoices the cooperative/driver weekly. Modelled 95% collection allows 5% leakage. Monitor off-platform switching and unpaid balances.
Why would an institution pay RWF 75,000?

For useful coordination, a maintained roster and trip records, if a budget holder judges the savings worth the cost. A signed paid trial is the evidence; ASYV is not presented as an existing customer.
What prevents a rider paying and the driver not coming?

Mova collects no passenger fare in advance. The customer pays the driver after the completed trip. This avoids a platform-held fare deposit but cannot guarantee arrival, eliminate fraud or resolve every external cash/MoMo dispute.
What about people without smartphones?
Use an authorized partner desk or phone assistance first. This is partly a human service and must fit the coordinator's limited support hours; USSD is a later costed option.
Is the pilot profitable?

Not in the base month-three scenario: its cash operating shortfall is RWF 84,800 before founder replacement cost and income tax. The pilot is a paid validation experiment, not a claimed profitable launch.
What if we get no institutional buyers?
Accounting for higher Google usage at the required volume, base cash break-even rises from about four to about 6.2 completed app trips per driver/day. Do not count unsigned subscriptions.
What are the biggest hidden costs?

Human support, regulatory/insurance requirements, lawful data hosting, driver verification, fee leakage, map reloads and founder labour. The detailed budget exposes each rather than calling the platform free.
What about students and safety?

The first operating pilot serves consenting adults only. No unaccompanied-minor service, ambulance promise or guaranteed-safe label is offered. Institutional permission and operator insurance/document checks are required.
What makes Mova difficult to copy?

The software features are easy to copy. A trusted local roster, useful partner relationships, consistent pickup operations and repeat usage could become advantages; they do not exist just because a prototype works.
What is already built and what still needs work?

Built: two-sided demo, plate selection, communication, negotiation simulation, server-timed approach, pickup-code flow and pay-after acknowledgement. Still needed: verified accounts, production data/security controls, real opted-in driver GPS, operating approvals and institutional service processes.
What exactly are you asking for?

A maximum RWF 2.85 million conditional 90-day pilot envelope. Release only RWF 150,000 for initial discovery first; that is part of the setup budget, not extra. Release later tranches only after compliance/partner gates and weekly spending review.
